meta.title: Questions about Open Bible Stories
meta.description: What Open Bible Stories is, how to read or download it in {count} languages, what the open license lets you do, and how to start a translation.

title: Questions about Open Bible Stories
intro: Short answers first. If your question isn't here, write to us.

questions.a: Open Bible Stories is 50 key stories of the Bible, from Creation to Revelation, for evangelism and discipleship, provided freely for translation and multi-media sharing in any language.

questions.q: Is Open Bible Stories a Bible translation?
questions.a:
No, the stories are a concise Scripture survey of the gospel, from Genesis to Revelation. Simplified language reduces the cognitive load on new learners by limiting the types of difficult translation issues they face. The content volume of all 50 stories is about the same as the book of Acts.

We train new translators to translate Open Bible Stories first because that work is less intimidating than translating the Bible itself. Open Bible Stories provides an ideal mechanism for introducing new teams to the fundamentals of good translation. Starting Bible translation with OBS gives a new translation team a great introduction to translation principles; it includes all the elements of team scripture drafting and checking, and it involves the use of key helps in the translation process. Translation teams complete the process in a matter of months, and the stories are immediately ready for use.

questions.q: How many languages is it available in?
questions.a: {count} languages have a published translation today, and more are in progress. Each one has its own page listing the stories, the formats that exist in that language, and the team that published it. See the Discover page for the full list.

questions.q: How do I read, listen to, or download it in my language?
questions.a: Open the Discover page, search for your language, and open its page. From there you can read every story, listen where a recording exists, watch where there is video, and download a PDF or the audio files. All digital versions are free online.

questions.q: Can I copy, print, adapt, or record these stories?
questions.a: Yes. Give as many copies of this book away as you want, without restriction. All digital versions are free online, and because of the open license we are using, you can even republish unfoldingWord® Open Bible Stories commercially anywhere in the world without paying royalties! The stories are released under the Creative Commons Attribution-ShareAlike 4.0 license (CC BY-SA 4.0). You may copy, print, record, broadcast, or adapt them, including commercially, provided you credit the original work and release what you make under the same license. Keep the unfoldingWord® trademark on unmodified copies, and remove it if you change or translate the work; say what you changed, and attribute it as “The original work by unfoldingWord is available from https://openbiblestories.org”. The illustrations are © Sweet Publishing and shared under CC BY-SA 3.0, so they carry their own attribution. The license page has the full text.

questions.q: How do I start a translation in my language?
questions.a: Start with the Translate page: it explains the process, the tools, and how to check a translation with the churches that will use it. Translation is done by teams from the language community, not for them, and unfoldingWord can help you find training and a network of other teams.

questions.q: Which stories tell the gospel, or the story of Abraham, or Easter?
questions.a: The stories run in biblical order, so they are easy to find by number. Creation and the fall are stories 1–3, God's covenant with Abraham begins at story 4, the Passover and the Exodus are stories 11–12, and the Old Testament closes with the promise of the Messiah in story 21. The life of Jesus runs from his birth in story 23 through his ministry and parables; the crucifixion is story 40, the resurrection story 41, and his return to heaven story 42. The church begins in story 43, and the last three stories, 48, 49 and 50, explain the gospel and Christ's return.

unfoldingWord® develops it together with the Door43 World Missions Community. Every translation is the work of a team from that language community, and each language page names the team that published it. The source files live on Door43, where anyone can see the current state of a translation.
